intro.author: James (1:1), traditionally identified as the brother of Jesus and leader of the Jerusalem church (Acts 15:13; Galatians 1:19). Some scholars think a later writer used his name.
intro.written: If by James, before his death in Jerusalem around AD 62, recorded by the historian Josephus; some date it as early as the 40s, which would make it one of the earliest New Testament writings
intro.audience: 'The twelve tribes which are scattered abroad' (1:1), most likely Jewish believers in Jesus living outside the land of Israel
intro.setting: The readers faced trials and poverty, and some were exploited by wealthy landowners (5:1-6). In their gatherings the rich were flattered and the poor slighted (2:1-4), and quarrels and harsh words were common. James writes in the style of Old Testament wisdom books like Proverbs, with short, vivid sayings, and his teaching often echoes Jesus' Sermon on the Mount.
intro.purpose: James calls believers to a genuine, mature faith that shows itself in endurance, care for the poor, controlled speech, humility and prayer.
intro.bigIdea: Real faith shows itself in the way we live.

outline.title: Trials, temptation and doing the word
